entries.title: Non-invertible symmetry enriched string net topological orders
entries.authors: Luisa Eck, Peter Huston, Kyle Kawagoe, David Penneys
entries.summary: Defines and constructs non-invertible symmetry enriched topological orders (NI-SETOs) using string net models via unitary fusion category inclusions and anyon condensation. All NI-SETOs can be realized in either model, with chiral examples on 3D Walker-Wang boundaries. Computes symmetry actions on anyons and defects using tube algebra.
entries.relevance: Directly relevant to Deepak's interest in topological order and category-theoretic approaches to quantum gravity. String net models and fusion categories are central to topological quantum computing and discrete quantum gravity.

entries.title: A multilevel tensor network compression technique for simulating Lindblad dynamics in superconducting circuits
entries.summary: A three-level tensor network compression scheme (purification, entanglement compression, quantics Fock representation) for simulating Lindblad dynamics of superconducting circuits. Achieves laptop-level performance for problems previously requiring supercomputers, demonstrated on cat qubits and transmon ionization.
entries.relevance: Highly relevant to Deepak's interest in tensor network methods and quantum computing. Practical simulation of open quantum systems is essential for superconducting quantum hardware design.

entries.title: Many-Body Quantum Chaos At All Time Scales
entries.authors: Antonio M. García-García, Lucas Sá, Jacobus J. M. Verbaarschot, Jie-Ping Zheng
entries.summary: Analytical study of quantum chaos across all time scales in the N-Majorana SYK model, combining scramblon formalism with random matrix theory. The OTOC and Green's functions exhibit dip-ramp-plateau patterns with deviations from ergodicity at late times due to local spectral correlations.
entries.relevance: The SYK model is a cornerstone of holography and quantum gravity research. Understanding chaos across all time scales is essential for black hole information and thermalization studies.

entries.title: Filtering out Erratic Observables: Wormholes from Gauging Nonlocal Symmetries
entries.summary: A novel construction of wormholes in 2+1 gravity by gauging nonlocal symmetries, showing that wormhole contributions emerge from filtering erratic observables in dual CFTs. Connects monodromy data, ensemble averaging, and quantum gate descriptions of wormhole states.
entries.relevance: Highly relevant to Deepak's interest in wormholes, quantum gravity, and holography. The nonlocal symmetry approach provides a novel perspective on the ER=EPR conjecture and ensemble averaging in holography.

entries.title: Stationary generalizations for the vacuum ring wormhole
entries.summary: Construction of stationary rotating generalizations of the ring wormhole, showing a transition from non-relativistic M~J^2 to relativistic Regge J=M^2 behavior. Solutions can be regularized via phantom scalar fields and approach extremal Kerr in a particular limit.
entries.relevance: The ring wormhole is a fascinating topological object connecting to Kerr black holes. The Regge relation and scalarization procedure connect to Deepak's interests in black hole physics and quantum gravity.

entries.title: Universal thermodynamic topological classes of the charged dRGT black string
entries.authors: Hao Chen, Meng-Yao Zhang, Yi Yang, Qihong Huang, Zheng-Wen Long
entries.summary: Topological classification of charged dRGT black string thermodynamics in canonical vs grand canonical ensembles, showing different stability classes (W^1+ vs W^0-) for large vs small black strings. The massive gravity-electromagnetic coupling is essential for nontrivial topology.
entries.relevance: Directly relevant to Deepak's research on black hole thermodynamics and quantum gravity. The topological classification approach and connection to massive gravity provides new insights into black string thermodynamics.

entries.title: Gravitational helicity in connection variables
entries.summary: A study of gravitational helicity in the connection formulation of GR, using Ashtekar variables and covariant phase space methods. The helicity is identified as a Noether charge for a duality symmetry and linked to the Nieh-Yan topological term.
entries.relevance: Directly relevant to Deepak's background in LQG. The use of Ashtekar variables and connection formulation connects to his expertise in loop quantum gravity. The Nieh-Yan term is important in the topological sector of gravity.

entries.title: Perturbative dynamics and relativistic effects of a dyonic Kalb-Ramond black hole
entries.summary: Comprehensive study of dyonic Kalb-Ramond black holes with Lorentz-violating antisymmetric tensor backgrounds, analyzing tidal effects, gravitational redshift, time delay, and quasinormal modes via sixth-order WKB method.
entries.relevance: The Lorentz-violating sector and dyonic charge structure are interesting extensions of standard black hole physics. The quasinormal mode analysis provides observable signatures for quantum gravity phenomenology.

entries.title: Lorentz-Violating (Regular) Black Holes in Einstein Gravity
entries.summary: A construction of regular black holes in Einstein gravity with Lorentz-violating conical asymptotics, using nonlinear electrodynamics. Includes Schwarzschild, Reissner-Nordström, Bardeen, and Hayward type regular black holes.
entries.relevance: Regular black holes are important in quantum gravity as they avoid singularities. The Lorentz-violating aspect connects to phenomenological quantum gravity approaches.

entries.title: GR from RG, $2d$ Example: JT-Gravity Induced from Renormalization Group Flow
entries.summary: A derivation of JT gravity from holographic RG flow in 2d CFTs, showing how the radial lapse function becomes the JT dilaton. The T\bar{T} deformation is recovered in the Fefferman-Graham limit.
entries.relevance: JT gravity is a key model in quantum gravity and holography. This first-principles derivation from RG flow provides a deeper understanding of how 2d gravity emerges from holographic renormalization.

entries.title: Krylov complexity has it all
entries.summary: Proof that Krylov complexity completely characterizes quantum operator dynamics, with an explicit recursive algorithm for extracting Lanczos coefficients from its Taylor expansion. Also clarifies the distinction from spread complexity.
entries.relevance: Krylov complexity has emerged as a key quantity in quantum chaos and holography. This proof of completeness and the recursive algorithm are important theoretical advances for understanding operator growth in quantum systems.

entries.title: Matching second-order classical and 1-loop quantum tensor power spectra in de Sitter spacetime
entries.summary: A study of second-order classical and 1-loop quantum corrections to the inflationary tensor power spectrum in de Sitter spacetime, identifying IR divergences in the classical part and proposing a non-perturbative renormalization procedure.
entries.relevance: Relevant to quantum cosmology and inflationary physics. The connection between classical scalar-induced gravitational waves and quantum loop corrections is important for understanding the early universe and primordial gravitational wave signals.

entries.title: Probing Spacetime Topology and Superposition with Accelerated Detectors
entries.summary: Investigates how spacetime topology (compactification) and superposition affect entanglement harvesting by accelerated detectors, finding that compactification boosts entanglement while superposition creates interference effects that expand the harvesting region.
entries.relevance: Entanglement in curved and superposed spacetimes bridges quantum information with quantum gravity, relevant to understanding how quantum correlations behave in non-trivial gravitational backgrounds.

entries.title: Universal Thermodynamic Topological Classes of BTZ Black Holes in Einstein and F(R) Gravity
entries.summary: Classifies BTZ black holes into universal thermodynamic topological classes, showing that F(R) gravity modifications and matter fields alter topological classifications, with ensemble choice also playing a key role.
entries.relevance: Black hole thermodynamics and topological classification are central to quantum gravity. This work extends topological understanding to modified gravity, relevant to holography and beyond-GR scenarios.

entries.title: Canonical quantization of massive vector field in Schwarzschild black hole background
entries.summary: Provides the first canonical quantization of a massive Proca vector field in Schwarzschild spacetime, deriving Hawking spectra and showing that a Proca condensate forms near the horizon.
entries.relevance: Quantum field theory in black hole backgrounds is foundational for Hawking radiation and black hole thermodynamics. The Proca field introduces new polarization dynamics that modify quantum observables near horizons.

entries.title: On a mixed-state extension of the holographic signal inequality
entries.summary: Generalizes a recent holographic entanglement inequality to mixed states and identifies holographic geometries that violate it, then conjectures a revised inequality for tripartite holographic states.
entries.relevance: Holographic entanglement inequalities constrain the allowed structure of quantum correlations in AdS/CFT. This work probes the boundaries of such constraints and their validity for mixed states.

entries.title: Thermal conformal partial waves from flat-space and defect CFT
entries.summary: Derives thermal conformal blocks from flat-space and defect CFT data using the shadow formalism, establishing a systematic correspondence that yields the thermal Casimir equation without chemical potentials.
entries.relevance: Conformal blocks are the building blocks of CFT correlation functions and holographic calculations. Understanding thermal blocks is essential for finite-temperature holography and black hole physics.

entries.title: Diffeomorphism-Like Symmetry in Gravitoelectromagnetism
entries.summary: Analyzes gauge symmetry in gravitoelectromagnetism within the Weyl formalism, deriving the propagator structure and showing that a Lorentz-like gauge preserves gauge independence while de Donder gauge is incompatible with the symmetry.
entries.relevance: Gravitoelectromagnetism provides a field-theoretic framework for understanding gravity-matter interactions. The gauge structure and Ward identities are foundational for consistent quantization and effective field theory approaches to gravity.

entries.title: Basis-Adaptive Sparse-State Simulation of Quantum Circuits
entries.summary: Introduces BASS, a basis-adaptive classical simulation algorithm for quantum circuits that rotates qubits into their natural-orbital basis before truncation, achieving up to an order of magnitude improvement in fidelity.
entries.relevance: Classical simulation of quantum circuits is essential for benchmarking and algorithm design. Adaptive basis techniques push the boundary of what can be efficiently simulated classically, directly relevant to quantum computing research.

entries.title: Deterministic Mapping of Topological Phases via Autoregressive Exogenous Neural Networks
entries.summary: Uses machine learning to map topological phase transitions in weak-measurement-induced geometric phases, achieving numerical-precision prediction and demonstrating deterministic structure in topological data.
entries.relevance: Machine learning for topological phases is an emerging frontier. This work shows that neural networks can discover exact mathematical relationships in topological quantum systems, relevant to quantum computing and condensed matter.

entries.title: Time Crystals on Quantum Devices
entries.summary: Reviews and classifies time crystal realizations on quantum devices, proposing a framework that includes discrete, continuous, topological, and quasiperiodic time-crystalline phases.
entries.relevance: Time crystals are a novel phase of matter with potential applications in quantum memory and precision sensing. This review surveys the rapidly evolving experimental landscape on quantum processors.

entries.title: Nonasymptotic bounds for quantum purity amplification
entries.summary: Derives finite-sample bounds for quantum purity amplification, showing how many copies of a noisy state are needed to extract k pure copies with high fidelity, independent of dimension.
entries.relevance: Purity amplification is a core primitive for quantum information processing. Nonasymptotic bounds are crucial for practical quantum computing where resources are limited.

entries.title: Quantum fluctuations and chaos in fully connected spin models
entries.summary: Uses the 2PI effective action formalism to study how quantum fluctuations regularize chaotic dynamics in a fully connected SU(3) spin model, bridging microscopic correlations and macroscopic behavior.
entries.relevance: Quantum chaos and thermalization are central to many-body physics and holography. This work provides a nonperturbative framework (2PI) for understanding how fluctuations modify chaotic classical trajectories.

entries.title: Algebras of order parameters in one-dimensional spin systems
entries.summary: Classifies string order parameters in 1D gapped phases using Lagrangian algebras in the Drinfel'd centre and tensor network techniques, extending the framework to symmetric mixed states.
entries.relevance: Topological order and symmetry-protected phases in 1D are foundational for understanding quantum phases of matter. The algebraic framework using Drinfel'd centres connects to categorical quantum mechanics and topological quantum computing.

entries.title: Autonomous oscillations in quantum electromechanics: tensor network treatment
entries.summary: Develops a tensor-network framework for autonomous electromechanical oscillations in nanoscale devices, demonstrating self-sustained oscillatory behavior without external periodic driving.
entries.relevance: Tensor network methods for open quantum systems are advancing rapidly. This work applies them to a challenging nanoscale electromechanics problem, relevant to quantum devices and nonequilibrium transport.

entries.title: Semiclassical foundation of universality in chaotic quantum circuits
entries.summary: Develops a periodic orbit theory for many-body chaotic quantum circuits, showing how random matrix universality emerges from synchronized time translations of subsystem periodic orbits.
entries.relevance: Quantum chaos and random matrix universality are key to understanding thermalization, information scrambling, and holographic duality. This semiclassical foundation bridges single-particle and many-body chaos.

entries.title: Thermal Casimir Effect in A Schwarzschild-like Wormhole Spacetime
entries.summary: Computes the thermal Casimir effect for a scalar field in a Schwarzschild-like wormhole, finding that thermal corrections become geometry-independent in the comoving frame while thermodynamic quantities show distinct temperature dependence.
entries.relevance: The Casimir effect in curved spacetime probes quantum vacuum structure in gravitational backgrounds, relevant to semiclassical quantum gravity and wormhole physics.

entries.title: Pseudorandom Dynamics in the SYK Model and Cryptographic Censorship in JT Gravity
entries.summary: Proves that the SYK model acts as an approximate unitary design and connects this property to horizon formation in JT gravity duals, establishing a concrete link between quantum complexity and black hole interior geometry.
entries.relevance: SYK/JT gravity is a cornerstone of quantum gravity research, connecting random matrix theory, holography, and black hole information. This work ties pseudorandomness to horizon formation — directly relevant to the black hole information paradox and complexity=volume.

entries.title: A pre-merger-informed spectral-level ringdown inference framework for black-hole spectroscopy
entries.summary: Introduces SPRING, a framework that incorporates pre-merger gravitational-wave data into ringdown inference to improve black hole spectroscopy without assuming specific theory-dependent QNM relations.
entries.relevance: Black hole spectroscopy tests the no-hair theorem and searches for beyond-GR effects. This method improves spectral inference by using pre-merger information — a significant methodological advance for LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA data analysis.

entries.title: Hairy Kiselev black hole with quintessential matter: thermodynamic properties, sparsity of Hawking radiation, and greybody factors
entries.authors: Faizuddin Ahmed, Fernando M. Belchior, Allan R. P. Moreira, Abdelmalek Bouzenada
entries.summary: Studies a hairy black hole with quintessence and cosmological constant, analyzing thermodynamic phase transitions, the intermittent nature of Hawking radiation, and greybody factors for scalar perturbations.
entries.relevance: Hairy black holes and their thermodynamics are important testbeds for quantum gravity effects. The analysis of Hawking radiation sparsity and greybody factors connects to observable signatures and black hole evaporation physics.

entries.title: Field Sources for Dark Matter Black Holes
entries.authors: G. Alencar, C. R. Muniz, Francisco Tello-Ortiz
entries.summary: Reconstructs regular black hole geometries from dark matter halo profiles using nonlinear electrodynamics, showing that halo distributions with finite central density yield de Sitter cores and Schwarzschild asymptotics.
entries.relevance: Bridges astrophysical dark matter phenomenology with regular black hole physics — relevant to understanding how dark matter environments modify black hole structure and to singularity resolution in quantum gravity.

entries.title: Electromagnetic emission from a black-to-white hole transition -- Photospheric emission
entries.summary: Proposes a photospheric emission model for gamma-ray bursts from black-to-white hole transitions and estimates the cosmological density of lunar-mass primordial black holes.
entries.relevance: Black-to-white hole transitions are predicted in loop quantum cosmology and other quantum gravity approaches as a resolution of singularities. The observational signatures calculated here provide a pathway to testing quantum gravitational effects.

entries.title: Grey-Body Factors and Thermodynamics of Asymptotically de Sitter Black Holes in Generalized Proca Theory
entries.authors: Bekir Can Lütfüoğlu, Javlon Rayimbaev, Nuriddin Kurbonov, Sardor Murodov, Faisal Javed
entries.summary: Computes greybody factors and absorption cross-sections for various test fields on vector-hair black holes in generalized Proca theory with effective de Sitter asymptotics, analyzing how field parameters modify transmission and thermodynamics.
entries.relevance: Modified gravity theories with hairy black holes offer alternatives to standard GR and probe how extra degrees of freedom alter black hole thermodynamics and observable spectra — relevant to beyond-GR phenomenology.

entries.title: Graviton scattering in the null surface formulation. Part III: Fourth-order Bondi shear and the tree-level amplitude
entries.authors: C. N. Kozameh, G. O. Depaola
entries.summary: Completes the NSF graviton scattering program by computing the fourth-order Bondi shear, proving UV finiteness at all loop orders, and deriving a generalized Jordan-Pauli relation for systematic perturbative calculations.
entries.relevance: The null surface formulation offers a nonperturbative framework for quantum gravity. The UV finiteness result is significant for understanding graviton scattering and the perturbative structure of quantum general relativity.

entries.title: Bulk Motion in Global AdS$_3$ from the Boundary Energy-Density Perspective
entries.summary: Shows that bulk null propagation in global AdS3 is precisely encoded in boundary CFT energy densities as periodic chiral peaks, establishing a direct bulk-boundary dictionary for localized excitations.
entries.relevance: AdS/CFT correspondence is central to holographic quantum gravity. This work provides a concrete mapping between bulk geodesics and boundary observables in global AdS3 — foundational for understanding holographic bulk reconstruction.

entries.title: Krylov Complexity for Plane Wave Matrix Model
entries.summary: Analyzes Krylov complexity in the BMN matrix model, finding linear scaling of Lanczos coefficients with mass deformation and quadratic early-time corrections to complexity growth.
entries.relevance: Krylov complexity is an emerging probe of quantum chaos and holographic complexity. The matrix model is a toy model for M-theory and AdS/CFT, making this relevant to quantum gravity and black hole interior dynamics.

entries.title: Homomorphic Quantum Error Correction
entries.summary: Establishes compatibility criteria between quantum homomorphic encryption and quantum error correction, analyzing stabilizer codes, CSS codes, and 3D color codes, and proposing solutions for non-Clifford gate implementation on encrypted encoded data.
entries.relevance: Combining quantum error correction with homomorphic encryption is essential for secure cloud quantum computing. This work provides the algebraic framework needed to process protected quantum data in server environments.

entries.title: A Variational Dissipative Framework for Quantum Algorithms
entries.authors: Yuan Yao, Ruipeng Xing, Yongjian Gu, Yiming Huang, Xiao Yuan
entries.summary: Introduces a variational framework that integrates engineered dissipative channels into quantum circuits via ancilla assistance, enabling preparation of mixed states and improving ground-state search and noise recovery.
entries.relevance: Dissipation is usually treated as noise to be eliminated, but this framework turns it into a resource for variational quantum algorithms. Relevant to NISQ-era quantum computing and open quantum systems control.

entries.title: Extracting Universal Entanglement Scaling from Mixed Fermionic Gaussian States via Entanglement Projected Entropy
entries.summary: Introduces entanglement projected entropy to extract universal entanglement scaling from mixed fermionic Gaussian states, successfully recovering conformal $c/3$ scaling in 1D and Dirac-governed scaling in 2D.
entries.relevance: Entanglement is central to many-body physics and quantum gravity (e.g., Ryu-Takayanagi). This work provides a practical tool for isolating entanglement from thermal noise in fermionic systems — highly relevant to quantum simulation and condensed matter.

entries.title: Local Impurity Induced Growth and Scrambling in Clean Free Fermions
entries.authors: Qucheng Gao, Vikram Ravindranath, Xiao Chen
entries.summary: Shows that a single impurity in a free fermion system can act as a branching source for operator growth and quantum scrambling, with feedback-driven transitions between saturation and sustained growth.
entries.relevance: Quantum scrambling and operator growth are key to understanding chaos, thermalization, and holography. This work reveals how minimal impurities generate complex dynamics — relevant to quantum information and many-body physics.

entries.title: Substitution modulated transition from semimetal to superconductor in ZrTe$_{2-x}$Se$_x$ with coexistence of nontrivial electronic topology
entries.authors: V. M. Fim, C. F. Schuch, L. R. de Faria, F. A. Santos, M. S. da Luz, S. S. Tsirkin, L. T. F. Eleno, A. J. S. Machado
entries.summary: Reports superconductivity up to 4.8 K in Se-substituted ZrTe2 with a phase diagram showing coexistence of Dirac semimetal and superconducting states, suggesting a platform for topological superconductivity.
entries.relevance: Topological superconductors hosting Majorana modes are key to topological quantum computing. The semimetal-superconductor coexistence with nontrivial Z2 topology makes this a promising experimental platform.

entries.title: Prediction of 1:1 kagome metals with superconductivity and band topology
entries.authors: Na Jiao, Shu-Xiang Qiao, Pan Zhou, Hong-Yan Lu, Ping Zhang
entries.summary: Predicts a family of 1:1 kagome metal stannides (MSn) that combine intrinsic phonon-mediated superconductivity with nontrivial topological band structures, identifying specific candidates for experimental synthesis.
entries.relevance: Kagome metals are at the frontier of topological quantum materials. Integrating superconductivity with nontrivial topology in a single material platform is a major goal for topological quantum computing and condensed matter physics.

entries.title: Negative entropy in scrambling black holes
entries.summary: Presents a microscopic statistical-mechanical foundation for interpreting the horizon area of a scrambling black hole as coherent information — equivalently negative conditional quantum entropy — within Hawking's pair-creation picture. Derives the entropy increase induced when an infalling object is absorbed and scrambled into the black hole's microscopic degrees of freedom, and shows that up to finite-resolution corrections, the black hole entropy can be identified with the negative conditional entropy of the created pairs.
entries.relevance: Connects black hole thermodynamics directly with quantum information theory via the concept of negative entropy in scrambling dynamics. Relevant to the black hole information paradox and the quantum mechanical nature of horizon entropy.

entries.title: Generalising gravitationally induced decoherence beyond linear environmental interactions in a microscopic quantum mechanical toy model
entries.authors: Max Joseph Fahn, Renata Ferrero, Kristina Giesel, Roman Kemper
entries.summary: Generalises a quantum mechanical toy model for gravitationally induced decoherence by extending the system-environment interaction beyond linear couplings to position operators. Formulates the interaction in terms of Weyl elements of the environment, allowing for a more general class of gravitational decoherence mechanisms in a microscopic setting.
entries.relevance: Advances the theoretical framework for understanding how gravity might induce decoherence at the quantum level — a key question at the interface of quantum mechanics and gravity. The generalised interaction model opens new avenues for testing gravitationally induced decoherence in tabletop experiments.

entries.title: Degenerate Bifurcations and Universal Relaxation Scaling in Black Hole Thermodynamics
entries.authors: Bidyut Hazarika, Mozib Bin Awal, Prabwal Phukon
entries.summary: Develops a dynamical systems approach to black hole thermodynamic criticality using bifurcation equations. Constructs an effective thermodynamic landscape in which black holes relax toward equilibrium fixed points, introducing a flow parameter interpreted as a phenomenological relaxation time that governs the approach toward equilibrium configurations.
entries.relevance: Provides a novel dynamical-systems perspective on black hole thermodynamic phase transitions, with potential implications for understanding how black holes respond to perturbations and settle into equilibrium. The universal relaxation scaling suggests deep structural properties of thermodynamic criticality in gravity.

entries.title: Non-monotonic evolution of multipartite entanglement under the Unruh effect
entries.authors: Shu-Min Wu, Si-Han Shang, Si-Yu Liu, Rui-Yang Xu, Qianqian Liu, Xiao-Li Huang
entries.summary: Investigates tetrapartite entanglement in a four-qubit Dicke state under relativistic motion using the Unruh-DeWitt detector model. Shows that entanglement exhibits a non-monotonic evolution — first decreasing and subsequently increasing toward a finite value as the acceleration grows — in contrast to the conventional monotonic degradation expected from the Unruh effect.
entries.relevance: Reveals unexpected non-monotonic entanglement dynamics under relativistic acceleration, challenging naive expectations about the Unruh effect's impact on quantum correlations. Important for quantum information in curved spacetime and relativistic quantum communication.

entries.title: Spacetime discreteness via consistent microscopic measurement
entries.summary: Proposes that spacetime discreteness can arise as a consequence of consistent microscopic measurement rather than being postulated a priori. Treats infinitesimal spacetime intervals as scale-dependent measurement outcomes, offering a model-independent approach to quantum spacetime discreteness that avoids reliance on specific microscopic structures.
entries.relevance: Offers a fresh perspective on spacetime discreteness grounded in measurement theory rather than model-dependent assumptions. Complementary to loop quantum gravity and other approaches that postulate discreteness at the Planck scale.

entries.title: Absorption and scattering spectra of massive scalar waves in charged regular black hole spacetimes
entries.authors: Marco A. A. Paula, Carolina L. Benone, Luís C. B. Crispino
entries.summary: Studies how massive scalar waves interact with charged regular black holes — geometries lacking curvature singularities — and compares the absorption and scattering spectra with those of standard Reissner-Nordström black holes. Computes greybody factors and scattering cross sections to characterize how regular black holes imprint distinct signatures on wave propagation.
entries.relevance: Regular black holes are important testbeds for quantum gravity effects that might resolve singularities. The wave spectra computed here provide observable signatures that could distinguish regular from singular black holes in future gravitational wave or astrophysical observations.

entries.title: Geodesics and Thermodynamics of a Schwarzschild Black Hole with Hernquist Dark Matter
entries.authors: A. R. P. Moreira, A. Bouzenada, F. M. Belchior, F. C. E. Lima
entries.summary: Constructs the metric for a Schwarzschild black hole immersed in a Hernquist dark matter halo and investigates null geodesics, photon dynamics, and the thermodynamic properties of the resulting spacetime. Examines how the dark matter environment modifies the black hole's geometric and thermodynamic behavior.

entries.title: Entanglement entropy across the dynamical phase transition in the quantum O(N) model

Quenches at and below the critical point generate gapless low-energy entanglement modes with logarithmic corrections governed by the dynamical exponent. The entanglement eigenmodes reveal characteristic signatures through their spatio-temporal structure and degeneracy properties.
entries.relevance: Connects quantum critical dynamics with entanglement structure in a tractable large-N model. Using Gaussian state methods, the authors analytically compute the logarithmic negativity and construct closed-form solutions for the localized modes carrying it, called "negativity cores." The results deepen understanding of entanglement in quantum field theory and suggest extensions to higher dimensions and fermionic fields.

The explicit analytical results in 1+1D provide a benchmark for entanglement measures in continuum quantum fields, with direct relevance to the ER=EPR conjecture and black hole entropy.

Under open boundaries, the edge spectral flow splits into two distinct events, with a neutral, spinful triplet-like excitation localized between them. The phase diagram shows filling-dependent topology with transitions between C=+2, C=-2, and C=+1 topological Mott pumps.

Growth quenches are proposed as a platform for non-equilibrium coherent phenomena.

digests.title: # arXiv Digest — 2026-05-18
digests.focus: quantum gravity, loop quantum gravity, black hole thermodynamics, quantum cosmology, quantum computing, condensed matter, topological order

entries.title: Quantum Gravity Beyond the Bulk
entries.summary: An infrared and asymptotic formulation of quantum gravity adapted to external observers. In an asymptotic proper-time gauge, the physical generator of evolution reduces to the Regge–Teitelboim boundary charge, so that quantum dynamics is governed by infrared gravitational configurations at spatial infinity. In the weak-field regime this leads naturally to a Born–Oppenheimer separation between slow asymptotic data and fast bulk fluctuations. Integrating out the latter induces a Berry connection on the space of admissible configurations, whose holonomy characterizes infrared-dressed gravitational states. Observable evolution is then governed by an infrared effective Hamiltonian obtained after integrating out fast bulk fluctuations, with the geometric (Berry) contribution entering as part of the resulting evolution operator on the space of asymptotic configurations. Tracing over unresolvable degrees of freedom induces a reduced density matrix whose entropy is dominated by global infrared holonomy sectors rather than local bulk dynamics.
entries.relevance: A novel infrared perspective on quantum gravity that shifts focus from bulk dynamics to boundary charges and Berry phases. The entanglement structure being dominated by infrared holonomy sectors rather than local bulk dynamics is a significant conceptual shift. Awarded an Honorable Mention in the 2026 Gravity Research Foundation Essay Competition.

entries.title: Loop Quantum Kaluza-Klein Cosmology and Inflation
entries.authors: Shengzhi Li, Yongge Ma, Faqiang Yuan, Xiangdong Zhang
entries.summary: Five-dimensional loop quantum Kaluza-Klein cosmology based on the symmetric reduction of the connection formulation of the full theory. The effective scalar constraint for the geometric sector is derived by systematic semi-classical analysis in both canonical and path-integral formulations, incorporating quantum fluctuations as a subleading-order correction. The resulting effective scalar constraint exhibits the correct classical limit and serves as the basis for investigating three distinct effective scenarios: (i) vacuum, (ii) minimally coupling with a scalar field, and (iii) coupling with dust. In all three scenarios, the big bang and potential past big rip singularities in the classical model are naturally resolved by including the leading-order quantum correction of holonomies. The visible universe undergoes a super-inflationary phase after overcoming the classical big bang singularity, during which the phenomenologically desired 55 e-folds can be achieved by appropriate initial conditions. When the subleading-order quantum fluctuation term is included as a constant, the evolutions in all three scenarios not only achieve sufficient inflation in the visible dimensions, but also exhibit re-collapse behaviors at certain large scales.
entries.relevance: Concrete bridge between loop quantum gravity and higher-dimensional cosmology. The resolution of both big-bang and big-rip singularities via holonomy corrections, combined with achieving sufficient e-folds of inflation, makes this a strong contribution to quantum cosmology phenomenology. The re-collapse behavior at large scales is an interesting prediction.

entries.title: Generating Rotation in a Snap
entries.authors: Soumangsu Chakraborty, Pierre Heidmann, Gela Patashuri
entries.summary: A new purely algebraic technique to generate rotation from arbitrary static solutions that asymptote to four- or five-dimensional Minkowski spacetime. The method does not require solving Einstein equations. It proceeds by transforming the static solution to AdS×S asymptotics, performing a coordinate shift to a uniformly rotating frame, and then transforming back to asymptotically flat spacetime. Implemented in five-dimensional minimal supergravity, though it applies more broadly to any framework admitting AdS×S geometries and relevant sigma-model transformations. As a first application, the Kerr and Myers-Perry black holes are recovered directly from Schwarzschild black holes. Applied to the linear class of static Weyl solutions, it yields the first linear ansatz describing an arbitrary number of non-extremal rotating and charged sources.
entries.relevance: Elegant algebraic shortcut for generating rotating solutions — recovering Kerr from Schwarzschild without solving field equations is a powerful demonstration. The extension to multi-source configurations suggests broad applicability for constructing complex rotating geometries.

entries.title: Kerroll Black Holes
entries.authors: Florian Ecker, Daniel Grumiller, Lucas Hörl, Mattéo Leturcq–Daligaux, Alfredo Pérez
entries.summary: Rotating black holes in Carroll gravity constructed via two distinct approaches. In one, the freedom in the Carroll compatible connection is exploited to encode rotation — constructing rotating solutions in magnetic Carroll gravity by dressing the Carroll-Schwarzschild black hole with a rotational charge. This solution is intrinsically Carrollian with no Lorentzian analog. In the other approach, an extension of magnetic Carroll gravity from general relativity in an odd-power expansion in the speed of light is constructed. This theory contains magnetic Carroll gravity as a subsector but has more physical degrees of freedom. It admits a Carroll analog of the Kerr black hole, referred to as the "Kerroll black hole," whose rotation appears as an intrinsically odd-power effect in the Carroll data. Conserved charges are computed for both theories.
entries.relevance: The "Kerroll" pun aside, this is a genuinely interesting exploration of Carrollian gravity — a non-relativistic limit of GR that has gained attention in holography and flat-space gravity. The existence of a Carroll analog of Kerr suggests deeper structure in the Carrollian limit than previously appreciated.

entries.title: A General Proof of Integer Rényi QNEC
entries.summary: Proof of the Rényi quantum null energy condition for all integer Rényi parameters n ≥ 2 for von Neumann algebras carrying a half-sided modular inclusion structure. The only assumption on the excited state is finiteness of its sandwiched Rényi divergence (SRD) relative to the vacuum. Concretely, for any σ-finite von Neumann algebra with such an inclusion, log-convexity is proved under the associated null-translation semigroup of the Kosaki Lⁿ norm of any normal positive functional with finite Lⁿ norm.
entries.relevance: Technical but important. The QNEC is a fundamental constraint in quantum field theory and quantum gravity. Extending it to integer Rényi indices with minimal assumptions strengthens the toolbox for proving energy conditions in infinite-dimensional settings.

entries.title: Dimensional Reduction of AdS₃ Chern-Simons Gravity
entries.authors: Goffredo Chirco, Lucio Vacchiano, Patrizia Vitale
entries.summary: A symmetry-reduced sector of AdS₃/ℤ₂ gravity formulated as an SO(2,2) Chern–Simons theory on a 3D manifold with toroidal boundary. The reduction is implemented by requiring a globally defined symmetry and restricting to the sector where the gauge connection is invariant along the symmetry flow. The resulting theory reduces to a two-dimensional BF-like model together with an induced one-dimensional boundary action. Two inequivalent boundary sectors arise from different boundary conditions for the parent 3D theory at the level of the variational principle. On the boundary subspace A_τ = Φ, the universal one-dimensional action reproduces the standard Drinfel'd–Sokolov reduction in JT gravity capturing Schwarzian boundary dynamics. On the generalized boundary A_τ = λ'Φ + u⁻¹∂_τ u, the same action yields a deformed Schwarzian functional with affine residual symmetry, naturally associated with a non-extremal or Rindler-type regime.
entries.relevance: Clean derivation of how 3D Chern-Simons gravity reduces to 2D BF + 1D boundary theory. The two boundary sectors — standard Schwarzian vs. deformed Schwarzian with affine symmetry — provide a nice organizing framework for understanding different near-boundary regimes.

entries.title: Anomalous Transport from Effective Field Theory
entries.authors: Rémy Larue, Amaury Marchon, Jérémie Quevillon, Diego Saviot
entries.summary: Systematic study of chiral effects using an Effective Field Theory framework. By integrating out a massive Dirac fermion at finite temperature in presence of vector and axial background fields, the currents and their anomalies are computed from the path-integral. Chiral effects previously considered separately naturally arise in a unified computation, including new mass corrections. The link between each anomalous transport effect and the anomalies is clearly established beyond the identification of their coefficients. These effects are sourced by the anomalous nature of the theory even in configurations where the anomaly itself vanishes. Both consistent and covariant anomalies are encapsulated in master formulae for the currents. At finite temperature, the physical currents cannot be inferred simply from the Chern-Simons terms whose divergence reproduce the chiral anomalies.
entries.relevance: Comprehensive EFT treatment of chiral anomalies and transport. The unified derivation with mass corrections, and the clarification that anomalous transport persists even when the anomaly vanishes locally, are valuable conceptual advances.

entries.title: Synthesis and Optimization of Encoding Circuits for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation
entries.authors: Tom Peham, Matthew Steinberg, Robert Wille, Sascha Heußen
entries.summary: Methods for synthesizing efficient encoders for arbitrary stabilizer codes. Encoder synthesis is formulated as a search over stabilizer tableaus, with greedy and rollout-based algorithms exploiting the freedom among stabilizer-equivalent realizations of the same encoding isometry. For code families with modular structure (generalized concatenated and holographic codes), large encoders are assembled from optimized local constituent encoders. SMT-based exact synthesis obtains optimal local circuits for small instances. Evaluated on holographic and quantum LDPC codes, obtaining improvements of up to 43% in two-qubit gate count and up to 70% in depth compared to recent methods and existing constructions. All methods are openly available as part of the Munich Quantum Toolkit.
entries.relevance: Encoder synthesis is a critical bottleneck for fault-tolerant quantum computing. The 43% reduction in gate count and 70% reduction in depth are substantial practical improvements. Open-source availability in the Munich Quantum Toolkit is a plus.

entries.title: Towards Deploying Optimistic Quantum Fourier Transforms
entries.summary: Architecture-algorithm co-design study of the Optimistic Quantum Fourier Transform (OQFT) under a surface-code fault-tolerant execution model for reconfigurable neutral-atom hardware. A hot-zone architecture decouples data storage from processing and dynamically routes mobile resource packages (magic-state factories, bridge qubits, and phase-gradient registers) to stationary data regions. Rotation insertions are routed via catalytic phase-gradient addition, and ripple-carry adders are heuristically micro-scheduled to patch-level moves. Under this model, Gidney and Cuccaro adders have similar space-time volume but require different parallelism levels. The five-layer OQFT shows a tunable parallelism/latency trade-off: two hot zones match serial-QFT latency, four hot zones roughly halve runtime, and additional hot zones asymptotically approach constant-time execution at substantial resource cost. Across 256-2048 bit instances, half-time performance requires about 500 additional logical ancillae and peak parallelism of 128 logical qubits.
entries.relevance: Concrete co-design study bridging algorithmic structure with hardware architecture for a core quantum subroutine. The explicit resource estimates (500 ancillae, 128 logical qubits for half-time at 2048 bits) are valuable for planning.

entries.title: Beyond Unitary Quantum Simulation
entries.authors: Michael Marthaler, Elias Zapusek, Florentin Reiter
entries.summary: Review discussing a broader perspective on quantum simulation motivated by the observation that naturally occurring quantum systems are rarely isolated and often reach physically relevant states only through relaxation, decoherence, and thermalization. Examines what is and is not known about exponential quantum advantage in chemistry, emphasizing that coherent Hamiltonian simulation provides the clearest formal case for speed-up while many open questions remain for realistic problems. Discusses how dissipation might be integrated into quantum chemistry on a fault-tolerant quantum computer, using recent proposals for chemically motivated dynamical simulation as a guiding vision. Highlights the practical appeal of open-system approaches to enhancing robustness of quantum algorithms.
entries.relevance: A timely corrective to the overemphasis on unitary ground-state simulation. The perspective that dissipation and thermalization are physically realistic and algorithmically useful is increasingly important as the field matures.

entries.title: Measurement-Efficient VQLS for Carleman-Linearized Nonlinear Dynamics
entries.summary: Hybrid quantum-classical pipelines for solving the Duffing equation leveraging Carleman linearization and the Variational Quantum Linear Solver (VQLS). Carleman linearization accurately approximates the weakly nonlinear Duffing equation with errors diminishing as truncation order increases. VQLS is deployed across IBM and Xanadu platforms with symmetry-grouped Hadamard Test evaluations under both global and local cost formulations. Distinct Hermitianizations are compared within a common cost framework, and hardware-efficient ansatz architectures are benchmarked under a fixed Hermitianization. Near-unity fidelity and vanishing relative residuals are achieved across block-banded test cases. The results show that topology-agnostic ansatz, optimized Hermitianization, and efficient cost formulation enable VQLS to recover quantum states proportional to classical solutions for Carleman-structured systems.
entries.relevance: Practical demonstration of solving nonlinear dynamics via quantum-classical hybrid methods. The cross-platform deployment (IBM and Xanadu) and near-unity fidelity results are promising for quantum-in-the-loop simulation.

entries.title: Unveiling Magnetic Frustration via the Elastocaloric Effect
entries.authors: Eric C. Andrade, Pedro M. Cônsoli, Matthias Vojta
entries.summary: The thermodynamic response of frustrated magnets to uniaxial strain is examined. Ising and Heisenberg models on spatially anisotropic triangular (and kagome for Ising) lattices are studied. The entropy as a function of temperature and strain is determined, and the elastic Grüneisen ratio η is computed. The Ising models can be strain-tuned into and out of classical spin-liquid phases, and η can become arbitrarily large at low temperature near the point of maximal frustration — a universal hallmark of an extensive ground-state entropy. In contrast, the spin-1/2 Heisenberg model is moderately frustrated and displays multiple T=0 phase transitions. These transitions dominate η at low T while the intermediate-T behavior is similar to the Ising model.
entries.relevance: The divergence of the Grüneisen ratio near maximal frustration is a clean thermodynamic signature that could guide experiments. The comparison between Ising and Heisenberg cases highlights how quantum fluctuations modify the frustration physics.

entries.title: Disorder-Driven Symmetry Suppression in a Magnetic Topological Insulator
entries.authors: Rikkie Joris, Heyi Xia, Ana Beatriz Pedro Fontes, Seul-Ki Bac, Sara Bey, Jiaqi Zhou, Zviadi Zarkua, Ahmed Samir Lotfy, Muhammed Saad, Philippe Ohresser, Margriet van Bael, Clement Merckling, Xinyu Liu, Francisco Molina-Lopez, Jean-Christophe Charlier, Jin Won Seo, Badih A. Assaf, Lino M. C. Pereira
entries.summary: Ion irradiation of the van der Waals magnetic topological insulator MnBi₂Te₄ modifies its magnetic and topological properties via collision cascades without chemical doping. Two regimes: at low fluence, cation antisite disorder leads to near-complete redistribution of Bi over cation sites while preserving long-range crystallographic order, accompanied by a transition from p-type to n-type transport. At high fluence, cation-anion intermixing drives formation of a previously unreported layer-disordered phase with a high density of van der Waals-specific planar defects including swapped bilayers. Despite significant structural disorder, partial periodic order persists. Magnetometry and X-ray spectroscopy show that the Mn high-spin state and antiferromagnetic interactions persist while magnetic anisotropy is strongly reduced. The anomalous Hall response is suppressed by over an order of magnitude, far exceeding the change in magnetization, indicating direct modification of Berry curvature.
entries.relevance: Direct Berry-curvature engineering via defect creation in a magnetic topological insulator. The suppression of the anomalous Hall response by >10× while preserving the magnetic ground state is a remarkable degree of control.

entries.title: Multifractal and Ergodic Properties of Conductance Fluctuations under Strong Disorder
entries.authors: Marcos A. A. de Sousa, Heitor R. Publio, Henrique A. de Lima, Adauto J. F. de Souza, Fernando A. Oliveira, Anderson L. R. Barbosa
entries.summary: Investigation of the multifractal and ergodic properties of the fictitious time series of conductance in two-dimensional tight-binding models under varying Anderson disorder. Using standard multifractal analysis, conductance fluctuations exhibit a transition from non-ergodic to ergodic behavior as disorder strength increases, as evidenced by the decay of the conductance correlation function. Multifractality persists in both regimes but becomes insensitive to shuffling in the strong-disorder (ergodic) regime, suggesting that distributional effects dominate temporal organization. In the weakly disordered (non-ergodic) regime, long-range correlations play a significant role. Results are robust against changes in lead geometry.
entries.relevance: The persistence of multifractality across the ergodic transition, combined with the shift from temporal-correlation-dominated to distribution-dominated behavior, provides a nuanced picture of how quantum transport statistics evolve with disorder.

entries.title: Fractal Analysis of Disordered Magnetic Systems
entries.authors: Klaus P. Hermann, Ismael S. S. Carrasco, Jairo R. L. de Almeida, Fernando A. Oliveira
entries.summary: Systematic investigation of magnetization, correlation functions, order parameter, and fractal dimensions in the Edwards-Anderson Hamiltonian as a function of disorder. The autocorrelation function for order-parameter fluctuations provides a framework for understanding the second-order phase transition at equilibrium. Recent work demonstrated that at T_c a fractal analysis is necessary for a complete description of the correlation function. Monte Carlo simulations validate analytical results and show how disorder alters critical exponents, giving rise to different universality classes. A subgroup of critical exponents and fractal dimensions is invariant with disorder, heralding a "strong universality class."
entries.relevance: The coexistence of disorder-dependent critical exponents (weak universality) with a disorder-invariant subgroup (strong universality) is a subtle and important result for understanding the taxonomy of universality in disordered systems.

entries.title: An Algebraic Resolution of the Firewall Paradox

entries.title: Parametrization of the primordial power spectrum in loop quantum cosmology

entries.title: C-Phase-Aware Compilation for Efficient Fault-Tolerant Quantum Execution

entries.title: Thermodynamics and optical aspects of ModMax black holes in higher order curvature gravity with quintessence dark energy
